candidates.name: overturemaps-py
candidates.what_it_holds: Official Overture Maps Foundation Python CLI (MIT license, 266 stars, 270 commits). Downloads Overture data for a bbox/region and a theme (places, buildings, transportation, divisions, base, addresses) and converts to GeoParquet/GeoJSON/etc. Places theme covers global POIs including accommodation/lodging categories (confirmed via schema repo cross-check, exact category list not extracted). Data underneath lives on S3/Azure as versioned monthly releases (STAC catalog), so pulling the same bbox at different Overture release dates gives a point-in-time-ish hotel/lodging POI count by city or metro.
candidates.why_useful: Gap #8/#9/#20: a free, global, monthly-versioned alternative to Inside Airbnb/AirDNA for counting STR-adjacent and hotel POIs by city, and for tracking new-supply growth (hotel openings, lodging POI density) as a cross-check on our Inside Airbnb listing counts. Also usable to build regional tourism-POI density controls (restaurants, attractions) as demand proxies.
candidates.license: MIT (tool); Overture Places data itself CC-BY / ODbL-style per source attribution
candidates.size_hint: Global places theme is hundreds of millions of POIs; per-city bbox pulls are small
candidates.last_activity: Active as of the fetch (270+ commits, current)

candidates.name: OvertureMaps/data
candidates.what_it_holds: Central Overture Maps release/documentation repo (MIT, 1.2k stars, 243 commits). Points to the actual Parquet data on S3/Azure via a STAC catalog, organized by theme (Addresses, Base, Buildings, Divisions, Places, Transportation) and release date; no data files committed to the repo itself.
candidates.why_useful: Confirms release cadence and access pattern for pulling historical Overture Places snapshots (point-in-time hotel/lodging POI counts) referenced by overturemaps-py above.
candidates.license: MIT (repo); underlying data attribution varies by source
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: Same underlying data as overturemaps-py above; listed separately because it documents the release/versioning mechanism needed for point-in-time pulls

candidates.name: OvertureMaps/schema
candidates.what_it_holds: Schema definitions (CC-BY-4.0, 212 stars, 1,595 commits) for all Overture themes including the `theme-places` package, which defines the category taxonomy used to classify POIs (would include accommodation/lodging/tourism categories, though exact list not extracted from this fetch — see docs.overturemaps.org for the full category tree).
candidates.why_useful: Needed to write a category filter (e.g. 'lodging', 'hotel', 'bed_and_breakfast') against overturemaps-py pulls; without the schema, category-based hotel counting from Overture isn't reproducible.

candidates.name: Foursquare Open Source Places (FSQ OS Places)
candidates.what_it_holds: Foursquare's open-sourced global places dataset (Apache 2.0 license), ~100M+ POI records (dataset docs cite up to ~1B rows counting historical/duplicate entries; ~239GB total across parquet files for places + a separate categories file). Commercial categories include hotels/lodging, restaurants, retail; 34 non-commercial categories (airports, cities, taxi stands, etc.) are flagged for filtering out. Distributed as Parquet on Hugging Face (gated download, free after accepting terms); no GitHub repo found for a companion access tool as of this check.
candidates.why_useful: Gap #20/#8/#9: a free, global, commercially-licensed (Apache 2.0) alternative POI census to build a worldwide hotel/lodging count by city and to identify non-Airbnb short-term-rental-adjacent venues (hostels, vacation rental offices) as a supply cross-check; could also proxy tourism-attraction density by market for demand normalization.
candidates.time_coverage: Single current snapshot (released 2024); unclear if historical snapshots are retained

candidates.name: Quattroshapes
candidates.what_it_holds: Foursquare-published global gazetteer of administrative boundaries and localities (CC-BY 2.0, 17 commits): admin level 0 (countries), 1 (states/provinces), 2 (counties), local admin areas, localities (cities/towns), and neighborhoods, in Shapefile (WGS84) and gzipped GeoJSON, sourced partly from Natural Earth v3.0.0 and government data. Over 1 million administrative/populated places; total ~30GB across files.
candidates.why_useful: Neighborhood-level boundaries for 13-city Inside Airbnb panel and any new market are otherwise ad hoc; this gives a free, global neighborhood polygon layer to join listings/reviews to sub-city geography for finer regional splits than city-level.
candidates.time_coverage: Static snapshot (project appears frozen, old but still usable as boundary reference)
candidates.size_hint: ~30 GB total, admin2 files ~1.5MB to local-admin ~467MB
candidates.last_activity: Old (17 commits, likely stale project from Foursquare's early open-data era)

candidates.name: pyrosm
candidates.what_it_holds: Python library (MIT, 438 stars, ~1,065 commits, Cython-accelerated) that parses OSM .osm.pbf extracts (e.g. Geofabrik regional dumps) directly into GeoPandas GeoDataFrames. Supports custom tag filters (including Overpass-style filters, so `tourism=hotel`/`tourism=guest_house` etc.) plus roads, buildings, land use, and boundaries. v0.10+ adds an out-of-core streaming engine for continental-scale files.
candidates.why_useful: Fastest available method to bulk-extract tourism/hotel POIs from Geofabrik country/region extracts for many cities at once, rather than one-by-one Overpass queries — directly serves the 'counting STR/hotel supply from maps' half of this theme.
candidates.time_coverage: Current OSM snapshot at pull time (historical PBF snapshots available separately from Geofabrik's internal history server, not this tool)

candidates.name: OSMPythonTools
candidates.what_it_holds: Python library (GPL-3.0, 487 stars, 177 commits) wrapping the Overpass API, Nominatim, and OSM API. Supports tag-based queries (e.g. `tourism=hotel`), reverse geocoding, GeoJSON export, and can track how a specific OSM object's tags changed over time (useful for a rough time series on individual hotel/venue records, though not scalable to full-city historical censuses since Overpass itself has no full history by default).
candidates.why_useful: Lower-effort alternative to pyrosm for smaller, per-city, live Overpass pulls of tourism=hotel/guest_house/apartment POIs when a full Geofabrik PBF isn't needed; the per-object history feature is a rare free way to see an individual venue's tag history.
candidates.last_activity: Maintained (noted activity 2017-2022 window in fetch, likely with intermittent updates since)

candidates.name: OSMnx
candidates.what_it_holds: Widely used Python package for downloading/modeling/analyzing OSM street networks, building footprints, transit, and 'urban amenities/points of interest' by place name or polygon.
candidates.why_useful: General-purpose alternative for pulling POI/amenity layers (including tourism/lodging tags) by named city or custom polygon, complementing pyrosm for smaller ad hoc pulls.
candidates.time_coverage: Current OSM snapshot at pull time

candidates.name: pyosmium
candidates.what_it_holds: Official Python bindings (BSD-2-Clause, 393 stars, 782 commits) for the libosmium C++ library, for fast low-level processing of OSM PBF files (including Geofabrik extracts and full history files with `.osh.pbf`).
candidates.why_useful: Lower-level building block than pyrosm; notably supports OSM's full-history PBF format, which is the closest thing to a point-in-time OSM POI census (can reconstruct what tourism=hotel tags existed as of a past date) — directly relevant to the point-in-time rule in this project.
candidates.time_coverage: Current + full OSM edit history when using history-enabled extracts

candidates.name: Who's On First data (gazetteer)
candidates.what_it_holds: Global gazetteer of places with stable 64-bit IDs, split into per-country repos (`whosonfirst-data-admin-{cc}`) and separate venue/POI repos (`whosonfirst-data-venue-*`) by country/region, as plain-text GeoJSON files (some via git-lfs for large countries). CC0 for original Mapzen work; attribution required for incorporated sources (GeoNames, Natural Earth).
candidates.why_useful: A free, versioned (git-history-backed) global venue/place gazetteer that can, in principle, be diffed over commit history for a rough point-in-time venue census — an alternative geography backbone to Overture/Foursquare for joining STR and hotel POIs to stable place IDs across markets.
candidates.time_coverage: Git history back to Mapzen's original ~2015-2017 work, updated intermittently since
candidates.license: CC0 (original work); mixed attribution for incorporated sources
candidates.last_activity: Low recent activity (111 commits on main tracking repo; per-country data repos vary)

candidates.name: geoBoundaries
candidates.what_it_holds: Global political administrative boundary polygons (CC BY 4.0 / ODbL-style, 947 commits, versioned releases e.g. v6.0.0) for all UN member states plus additional entities, ~300M vertices across hundreds of thousands of geometries, distributed via GitHub, API, and Python/R packages; tracks boundary changes since 2016.
candidates.why_useful: Standardized, versioned admin-boundary layer to aggregate any POI/hotel-count dataset (Overture, OSM, Foursquare) up to consistent country/state/metro units across markets — a cleaner alternative to ad hoc boundary files for the regional (NA/EMEA/LatAm/APAC) splits this pitch needs.
candidates.time_coverage: Versioned since 2016, with dated releases enabling point-in-time boundary use
candidates.last_activity: Active (latest tagged release noted v6.0.0, Sep 2023)

candidates.name: regional (OSM extract splitting scripts)
candidates.what_it_holds: Shell/Python scripts (43 stars, 32 commits) to cut custom polygon extracts from a full OSM planet file and keep them updated with incremental diffs — a manual, self-hosted alternative to relying solely on Geofabrik's pre-cut regional extracts.
candidates.why_useful: Marginal: useful only if Geofabrik's existing city/region cuts don't match the exact metro polygons needed for a market (e.g. a custom Airbnb-market boundary); otherwise Geofabrik's own downloads are simpler.
candidates.time_coverage: Current + incremental diffs going forward from setup date
candidates.last_activity: Low (32 commits total, appears largely dormant)

notes: Both dedicated tool budgets were constrained in this run: WebSearch had already exhausted its shared 200-call session budget before any of my three queries returned results (this appears to be a session-wide quota shared across many parallel scout agents, not something specific to this theme), and github.com/search was 429-rate-limited (retry-after 3600s) after two attempts, so I could not browse GitHub's own search index at all. DuckDuckGo HTML search returned a CAPTCHA wall both times, and Bing's rendered result snippets did not surface indexed content beyond generic github.com navigation pages. I compensated by using WebFetch directly against ~18 specific repo URLs recalled from general knowledge of the OSM/Overture/Foursquare open-geodata ecosystem, verifying each one that resolved (7 came back 404/renamed and are omitted below: geofabrik/sophox, foursquare/fsq-os-places-utils, opentripmap/opentripmap, placekey/placekey-py, safegraph/safegraph_py, and two Overture URL variants that needed the no-hyphen 'overturemaps-py' spelling). Coverage gaps for a future scout with working search: (1) I could not find a GitHub-hosted academic replication package that explicitly counts STR-vs-hotel supply from OSM/Overture and compares to Inside Airbnb — this specific angle (gap #2/#8) is very likely to exist as a paper-plus-repo and is worth a dedicated search once GitHub search or WebSearch budget resets; (2) Geofabrik itself has no GitHub org with code — it is purely a download site (download.geofabrik.de) — so 'Geofabrik tooling' in practice means third-party clients like pyrosm/pyosmium/regional above, not anything hosted by Geofabrik; (3) I could not confirm whether Foursquare publishes historical/point-in-time snapshots of fsq-os-places (only a single current release was found) — worth checking Hugging Face's dataset versioning tab directly; (4) SafeGraph and Placekey (both potentially relevant to gap #17 methods and gap #5 foot-traffic-as-engagement-proxy) could not be reached at the URLs I guessed and deserve a proper search pass, since SafeGraph historically published free hotel/lodging foot-traffic patterns data relevant to occupancy proxies.
